summary: Revalidated Ternium after its Q2 2026 release and the merged upper-band, overbought-RSI and volume alerts. Steel shipments, Mexican demand, margins and attributable earnings improved, while operating cash flow remained below capex after a large working-capital build and the company moved to modest net debt. A scenario-complete cyclical assessment values the ADS at USD 28 bear, USD 50 base and USD 78 bull with 25%/50%/25% probabilities. The USD 51.50 weighted value is below the USD 53.71 mark, so the canonical conclusion remains Hold / Watch with no strategy. Created exactly one dependent nearshoring-idea refresh.

evidence.claim: Ternium reported Q2 steel shipments of 3.858 million tonnes, net sales of USD 4.340 billion, adjusted EBITDA of USD 717 million at a 17% margin, USD 344 million of equity-holder net income and USD 1.75 EPS per ADS. Operating cash flow was USD 256 million, capex USD 431 million and June-end net debt USD 112 million; management described the Pesquería steel shop as progressing on schedule and expected Q3 adjusted EBITDA to rise.
The retained primary filing provides the current buildout framing and revised early-2027 operating expectation used to preserve commissioning and project-return risk.

The prior-quarter filing establishes the sequential baseline of USD 479 million adjusted EBITDA, USD 213 million equity-holder earnings, USD 217 million operating cash flow, USD 406 million capex and USD 327 million net cash.
